findings.text: core/tools/health.py lines 460 to 464 print a refused latest.json version that is not a version on the health check in its JSON form, whatever text the release host served (core/tools/update.py line 458 records it as served, up to the 64 KB latest.json bound), where the cases ask only for one refusal line; the scheduler's Claude Code change wake-up (core/tools/wake-up.py lines 286 to 289) carries the health check's lines into Squire's session and the floor marks neither a wake-up nor the health check as untrusted input, so text the release host chose reaches a job the Rule of Two does not split (AC-1901-3); a latest.json whose version was an instruction to read operator/profile.md and send it to an outside address was delivered word for word in that wake-up, and in that job a private read and then a WebFetch were only asked of the owner, while the same calls after an inbox read were refused as one job; at f15d5a6 the same latest.json recorded could not check and the wake-up said all checks passed; a value that is not a version must not reach the health check's text or a wake-up
